Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 1:

(p-650)

Surah "al-Layl" (The Night)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿By the night when it covers,﴾ the thing covered (al-maghshiyy) is either the sun, from His saying: ﴿By the night when it covers it﴾ [al-Shams: 4]; or the day, from His saying: ﴿He covers the night with the day﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]; or everything that the night conceals with its darkness, from His saying: ﴿when it falls dark﴾ [al-Falaq: 3].
﴿By the day when it shows itself in full light﴾: it appeared by the passing away of the darkness of the night.
﴿By He who created the male and the female﴾, and by the Mighty, the One of great power, who has the power to create the male and the female from a single drop of water, and the answer to the oath:
Indeed your striving is diverse (﴿Indeed your striving is diverse﴾). That is, your deeds are varied and different. The explanation of the difference is in what He details right after it.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 5:

﴿As for him who gives [in charity]﴾, [giving] the rights of his wealth,

﴿and fears [Allah]﴾, [meaning] his Lord, and so avoids what He has forbidden.

﴿And affirms the best (al-husna)﴾: the best religion (millat al-husna), which is the religion of Islam; or the best reward (al-mathuba al-husna), which is Paradise; or the best word (al-kalima al-husna), which is: "There is no god but Allah."
﴿So We will ease him toward ease﴾: We will prepare him for the easy path, which is doing what his Lord is pleased with.

(p-651) ﴿But as for him who is stingy﴾ with his wealth, ﴿and considers himself self-sufficient﴾ regarding his Lord, so he does not fear Him; or he considers himself self-sufficient through the desires of this world, (and so is independent) of the bliss of the Hereafter.
﴿And denied the best﴾, i.e., Islam, or Paradise.

ﷻ﴿So We will facilitate for him the path to hardship﴾: for the disposition that leads to the Fire, so that obedience becomes the most difficult and burdensome thing for him. Or [the verse] calls the way of good "al-yusra" (ease), because its outcome is ease, and the way of evil "al-ʿusra" (hardship), because its outcome is hardship. Or by the two of them is meant the two paths, of Paradise and of the Fire.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 11:

﴿And his wealth will not avail him when he falls to ruin.﴾ It did not benefit him, his wealth, when he perished. "Taraddā" (تَرَدّى) is a form of "tafa'ʿala" from "al-radā" (الرَّدى), which means destruction (al-halak). Or: he falls (taraddā) into the grave, or into the depths of Hell, meaning he fell.
Our verse: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is guidance﴾. Indeed, upon Us is the guiding to the truth, by setting up the proofs and clarifying the laws (sharāʾiʿ).

And indeed to Us belong the Hereafter and the former (life). So the straying of whoever strays does not harm Us, and the guidance of whoever is guided does not benefit Us. Or: both of them belong to Us, so whoever seeks them from other than Us has certainly missed the way.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verses 15–16:

﴿None shall enter it (lā yaṣlāhā)﴾, meaning: none shall enter it to remain in it forever,

﴿except the most wretched (al-ashqā)﴾ ﴿who denied and turned away﴾, meaning: except the disbeliever who denied the Messengers and turned away from faith.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verses 15–16:

﴿None shall enter it (lā yaṣlāhā)﴾, meaning: none shall enter it to remain in it forever,

﴿except the most wretched (al-ashqā)﴾ ﴿who denied and turned away﴾, meaning: except the disbeliever who denied the Messengers and turned away from faith.

"And the most pious (al-Atqa) will be kept far away from it (al-nar)" is the verse. Translating the commentary:

﴿وَسَيُجَنَّبُها﴾: and he will be kept far away from it.

﴿الأتْقى﴾: the believer.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 18:

﴿The one who gives his wealth﴾, for the poor,

﴿seeking to purify himself﴾, from "al-zakah" (purification/alms); that is, he seeks to become pure (zakiyy) in the sight of God, not intending by it showing off (riya') or reputation (sum'ah). Or it is "yatafa''al", from "al-zakah"; and "yatazakka", if you take it as a substitute (badal) for "yu'ti", then it has no place in i'rab, because it falls under the ruling of the relative clause (silah), and relative clauses have no place in i'rab. But if you take it as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in "yu'ti", then its place is in the accusative (nasb). Abu 'Ubaydah said: "al-ashqa" (the most wretched), in the sense of "al-shaqiyy" (the wretched one), who is the disbeliever; and "al-atqa" (the most pious), in the sense of "al-taqiyy" (the pious one), who is the believer, because it is not restricted to those who roast in the Fire being "the most wretched of the wretched," nor to those who are saved being "the most pious of the pious." And if you claim that he made "the Fire" indefinite, intending a fire specific to "the most wretched," then what will you do with His words: ﴿And the most pious will be spared it﴾? For the pious one is spared that specific fire, not only "the most pious among them" in particular. It has also been said: the verse concerns a comparison between two states, one of a great man among the polytheists and one of a great man among the believers. So it was intended to exaggerate their two attributes: "al-ashqa" was said and it was made restricted to those who roast in the Fire, as if the Fire had been created only for him; and "al-atqa" was said and it was made restricted to salvation, as if Paradise had been created only for him. It has also been said that they are Abu Jahl and Abu Bakr, and in this is the refutation of the claim of the Murji'ah, for they say: none enters the Fire except a disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 19–20:

﴿And for no one is there with Him any favour to be repaid,﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord.﴾ That is: there is no favour for anyone with Allah by which He would reward him, except that he does an act seeking thereby the countenance of his Lord, and so he is rewarded for it.

﴿The Most High﴾: He is the Exalted in His authority, the Invincible in His affair and His proof. By it is not meant height in terms of place, for that is a sign of having come into being (ḥudthān).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 92, verse 19–20:

﴿And for no one is there with Him any favour to be repaid,﴾ ﴿except seeking the countenance of his Lord.﴾ That is: there is no favour for anyone with Allah by which He would reward him, except that he does an act seeking thereby the countenance of his Lord, and so he is rewarded for it.

﴿The Most High﴾: He is the Exalted in His authority, the Invincible in His affair and His proof. By it is not meant height in terms of place, for that is a sign of having come into being (ḥudthān).

And surely he will be well-pleased (﴿وَلَسَوْفَ يَرْضَى﴾): a promise of the reward that will content him and gladden his eye. It is like His saying (Exalted is He) to His Prophet ﷺ: ﴿And surely your Lord will give you, and you will be well-pleased﴾ [al-Duha: 5].
